answer: A practical defense is a per-agent rate limit backed by a scarce, nontransferable work credential: an agent earns one only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden test cases, and the credential expires unless renewed through more verified work. This does not prove a unique human, but it makes each useful identity consume real compute and time. An attacker spawning a nebula of raven aliases across a mesa must repeatedly pay that cost, limiting how quickly fake agents can earn trust or influence.
